screens.title: The output-size formula
screens.prose: For an input side $n$, kernel $k$, padding $p$ and stride $s$, $$\text{out} = \left\lfloor \frac{n + 2p - k}{s} \right\rfloor + 1.$$ The padded side is $n + 2p$; the last start is at most $n + 2p - k$; starts come every $s$.

byKey.pad-once: Padding goes on both sides: add $2p = 4$.
byKey.same: Padding 2 keeps the size only at stride 1.

explain.text: $32 + 4 - 5 = 31$, so starts run 0, 2, ..., 30: that is $\lfloor 31/2 \rfloor + 1 = 16$ of them.

lines.text: Padding adds $p$ zeros at each end, so the side is $n + 2p$.
A window starting at column $c$ covers $c$ to $c + k - 1$, so it fits when $c \le n + 2p - k$.
Starts are $0, s, 2s, \dots$: start $c = js$ fits when $j \le (n + 2p - k)/s$.
So $j$ runs from 0 to $\lfloor (n + 2p - k)/s \rfloor$, which is $\lfloor (n + 2p - k)/s \rfloor + 1$ stops.
Padding adds $p$ zeros in all, so the side is $n + p$.
lines.why: Padding $p$ puts $p$ zeros on each side, $2p$ in all.

screens.title: "Same" padding
screens.prose: With stride 1, the output keeps the input size when $n + 2p - k + 1 = n$, so $p = (k - 1)/2$. This is **same** padding, and it needs an odd kernel.

byKey.k-1: That is the total padding, $2p$. Each side gets half.

explain.text: $2p = k - 1 = 4$, so $p = 2$ on each side. An even kernel would need $p = 1.5$, which is why "same" kernels are odd.

screens.prose: A stride of 2 skips every other start in both directions, so the map shrinks by about half on each side and holds about a quarter of the values.

screens.title: The formula in code
screens.prose: Write `out_size(n, k, p, s)`, returning a whole number.
screens.question: Write `out_size`.

widget.solution:
def out_size(n, k, p, s):
    return (n + 2 * p - k) // s + 1

widget.solution:
import numpy as np


def conv2d(img, k, stride, pad):
    img = np.asarray(img, dtype=float)
    k = np.asarray(k, dtype=float)
    x = np.pad(img, pad)
    kh, kw = k.shape
    oh = (x.shape[0] - kh) // stride + 1
    ow = (x.shape[1] - kw) // stride + 1
    out = np.zeros((oh, ow))
    for i in range(oh):
        for j in range(ow):
            r, c = i * stride, j * stride
            out[i, j] = np.sum(x[r:r + kh, c:c + kw] * k)
    return out

tests.setup: r = np.random.default_rng(51); x = r.standard_normal((9, 9)); k = r.standard_normal((3, 3)); s, p = 2, 1
tests.call: bool(np.allclose(conv2d(x, k, s, p), np.einsum('ijab,ab->ij', np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(np.pad(x, p), k.shape)[::s, ::s], k)))

r = np.random.default_rng(53); x = r.standard_normal((6, 6)); k = r.standard_normal((3, 3)); s, p = 1, 1
tests.call: bool(np.allclose(conv2d(x, k, s, p), np.einsum('ijab,ab->ij', np.lib.stride_tricks.sliding_window_view(np.pad(x, p), k.shape)[::s, ::s], k)))

ideas: Padding $p$ adds $p$ zeros on each side; stride $s$ is the jump between windows; along each side $\text{out} = \lfloor (n + 2p - k)/s \rfloor + 1$.
"Same" padding $p = (k - 1)/2$ keeps the size at stride 1 and needs an odd kernel; stride 2 roughly halves each side.
When $s$ does not divide $n + 2p - k$, the last columns are dropped without warning; a stride longer than the kernel skips input.
